items.title: Section: Delight from Precept Purity, and Delight from Overcoming Obstructions

items.zh: 汝於如是正觀察時，若自了知戒蘊清淨，雖不作思：我當發起清淨無悔。然其法爾尸羅淨者，定生如是清淨無悔。若起如是清淨無悔，雖不作思：我起歡悅。然其法爾無有悔者，定生歡悅。如是且於一種歡悅所依處所，汝應生起清淨無悔為先歡悅。
items.en: "When you examine yourself in this way, if you know for yourself that your moral discipline is pure, then even without deliberately intending to arouse a sense of clean, regret-free conscience, purity of precepts naturally, of itself, gives rise to just such a regret-free conscience. And should such a regret-free conscience arise, then even without deliberately intending contentment, freedom from regret naturally, of itself, gives rise to contentment. Thus, from this one basis alone, you should give rise to contentment led by a clean, regret-free conscience."

items.zh: 復於除障喜悅處所，當生喜悅。謂我今者尸羅清淨，有力有能安住世尊所制學處；於現法中，能得未得、能觸未觸、能證未證。由是處所生喜悅意。若汝獲得前後所證少分差別，即由如是增上力故，於他圓滿所證差別，謂諸如來、或聖弟子，及自後時所證差別，當生信解，發喜悅意。如是行相諸適悅意，先名歡悅，今名喜悅。總名悅意。
items.en: "Further, from the basis of overcoming obstructions, gladness arises: 'My precepts are now pure; I have the strength and capacity to abide by what the World-Honoured One has laid down. In this very life, I am able to attain what is not yet attained, to touch what is not yet touched, to realise what is not yet realised.' From this basis, gladness arises. If you have attained some small measure of progress, comparing what you were before to what you are now … then, by that same empowering force, regarding the perfected attainment of others … and your own future attainment as well, confidence and understanding arise, and gladness follows." Such states of ease are, at first, called contentment, and now called gladness — together called ease of mind.

items.zh: 如是名為取欣樂相。取是相已，復應教授。告言：賢首！汝由如是厭離相故，調練其心；復由如是欣樂相故，滋潤其心，汝於斷滅世間貪憂應多安住。隨於彼彼所緣境界勤修加行，或奢摩他品、或毘鉢舍那品；即於彼彼所緣境界，當令心住內住、等住。汝當獲得身心輕安及一境性。

items.title: Section: The Mark of Danger — the Ten Marks, Eight Thoughts, and Five Hindrances Revisited

items.zh: 汝若如是背諸黑品，向諸白品，由調練心、滋潤心故，復應數數取過患相。謂於所有諸相、尋思、及隨煩惱，取過患相。言諸相者，謂色等十相。言尋思者，謂欲等八。隨煩惱者，謂貪欲等五。
items.en: "Having thus turned away from the dark category and towards the bright, through taming and moistening the mind, you should further, again and again, grasp the mark of danger — that is, grasp the mark of danger with respect to all marks, discursive thoughts, and secondary afflictions. By 'marks' is meant the ten marks, beginning with form. By 'discursive thoughts' is meant the eight, beginning with desire. By 'secondary afflictions' is meant the five, beginning with craving."

items.zh: 如是諸相，能令其心作用遽務；如是尋思，能令其心思慕躁擾；如是隨煩惱，能令其心恒不寂靜。若心作用，諸相所作；思慕躁擾，尋思所作；恒不寂靜，隨煩惱所作；由是令心苦惱而住。是故如是諸相、尋思及隨煩惱，是苦非聖，能引無義。令心散動、令心躁擾、令心染
items.en: These marks cause the mind to become hurried and preoccupied; these discursive thoughts cause the mind to become restless with longing; these secondary afflictions cause the mind to remain forever unsettled … through this, the mind dwells in distress. Therefore, these marks, discursive thoughts, and secondary afflictions are suffering, not the state of the noble ones, and lead to what is without benefit — causing the mind to scatter, causing the mind to become agitated, causing the mind to become defiled.

items.title: The Mark of Non-Disturbance Opens: Six Qualities of a Settled Mind

items.zh: 又汝應依心一境性、心安住性、心無亂性，以六種行正取其相。
items.en: "Further, relying on one-pointedness of mind, the mind's abiding nature, and the mind's undisturbed nature, you should rightly grasp its mark through six aspects."

items.zh: 何等為六？一、無相想；二、於無相中，無作用想；三、無分別想；四、於無分別中，無所思慕無躁擾想；五、寂靜想；六、於寂靜中，離諸燒惱寂滅樂想。
items.en: What are the six? First, the perception of markless-ness. Second, within marklessness, the perception of no [distracting] function. Third, the perception of non-discrimination. Fourth, within non-discrimination, the perception of freedom from longing and agitation. Fifth, the perception of tranquility. Sixth, within tranquility, the perception of the bliss of cessation, free of every affliction.

items.title: Section: The Marks of Brightness and of Discerning the Object

items.zh: 汝取如是過患相已，復應數數取光明相。謂或燈明、或大火明、或日輪明、或月輪明。
items.en: "Having grasped the mark of danger in this way, you should further, again and again, grasp the mark of brightness — that is, the brightness of a lamp, of a great fire, of the sun's disk, or of the moon's disk."

items.zh: 既取如是光明相已，復詣塚間取青瘀相，廣說乃至取骨鎖相。汝若不能往詣塚間，當取彩畫、木、石所作如是諸相。
items.en: "Having grasped the mark of brightness in this way, you should further go to a charnel ground and grasp the mark of discoloration, and so on at length, up through grasping the mark of the bone-chain. If you are unable to go to a charnel ground, you should instead grasp such marks as rendered in painting, wood, or stone."

items.title: Applying the Marks in Seated Practice

items.zh: 取是相已，還所住處，或阿練若、或林樹下、或空閑室、或在大床、或小繩床、或草葉座，先洗足已，結跏趺坐，端身正願，安住背念。先於一境令心不散，繫念在前。復於其中，依六種想作意思惟。
items.en: "Having grasped these marks, return to your dwelling place — a forest hermitage, beneath a grove of trees, an unoccupied room … having first washed your feet, sit cross-legged, with an erect body and right aspiration, abiding in mindfulness turned away, first fixing the mind unwaveringly on a single object, holding it in mindfulness. And within this, direct your attention according to the six perceptions."

items.zh: 謂無相想、無分別想、寂靜想、無作用想、無所思慕無躁擾想、離諸燒惱寂滅樂想。

items.title: Section: Discerning Disturbed from Undisturbed Mind

items.zh: 又於其中，汝當審諦周遍了知亂不亂相，分明現前。如如審諦周遍了知亂不亂相，如是如是汝能了知諸相、尋思、隨煩惱中所有亂相，及能了知心一境性隨六想修諸不亂相。又汝於此亂不亂相，如是如是審諦了知，便能安住一所緣境，亦能安住內心寂止，諸心相續、諸心流注，前後一味，無相、無分別，寂靜而轉。
items.en: "Further, within this, you should carefully and thoroughly know the disturbed and undisturbed marks, clearly present before you … And to whatever degree you carefully and thoroughly know these disturbed and undisturbed marks, to that degree you become able to abide in a single object, and able to abide in inward stillness — mind continuing upon mind, mind flowing upon mind, one taste from beginning to end, free of marks, free of discursive thought, proceeding in tranquility."

items.zh: 又若汝心雖得寂止，由失念故，及由串習諸相、尋思、隨煩惱等諸過失故，如鏡中面所緣影像，數現在前；隨所生起，即於其中當更修習不念作意。謂先所見諸過患相增上力故，即於如是所緣境相，由所修習不念作意，除遣散滅，當令畢竟不現在前。賢首當知！如是所緣甚為微細，難可通達。汝應發起猛利樂欲，為求通達，發勤精進。

blocks.text: The rest of the five marks, and the moment the student sits down to practise. A few short passages are untranslated.

If the precepts are pure, "even without deliberately intending it, purity of precepts naturally gives rise to a regret-free conscience". From overcoming obstructions, gladness: "In this very life, I am able to attain the unattained." Venerable Miào Jìng: such ease is at first "contentment", then "gladness".

Grasp the danger in the ten distracting marks, the eight thoughts, the hindrances: "these marks make the mind hurried; these thoughts make it restless with longing; these afflictions keep it forever unsettled". They are "suffering, not the state of the noble".

Relying on one-pointedness: the perception of marklessness; within it, of no function; of non-discrimination; within it, of freedom from longing and agitation; of tranquility; within it, "of the bliss of cessation, free of all affliction".

The brightness of "a lamp, a great fire, the sun's disk, or the moon's". Then go to a charnel ground and grasp the marks of discoloration up to the bone chain; "if you cannot go, grasp such marks as rendered in painting, wood, or stone".

"Return to your dwelling; having first washed your feet, sit cross-legged, body erect, right aspiration, mindfulness turned away; first fix the mind unwaveringly on a single object." Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the first stage, inward abiding.
"Carefully know the disturbed and undisturbed marks", and the mind becomes able to abide on a single object.

quiz.q: With pure precepts, "without deliberately intending it, regret-free conscience naturally arises." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: no need to think it — keep pure precepts and there's no regret
quiz.why: "Even without deliberately intending to arouse a regret-free conscience, purity of precepts naturally gives rise to just such a conscience." Venerable Miào Jìng: I don't think about it — if my precepts are pure, I won't regret; no need to think it.

quiz.q: "From overcoming obstructions, gladness arises." Which obstructions, according to the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: the five hindrances; Cháng Bǎi more broadly: timidity, covering, discursive thought, self-conceit
quiz.why: "Further, from the basis of overcoming obstructions, gladness arises." Venerable Miào Jìng: overcoming obstructions means dispelling the five hindrances; able to do so, the mind is glad. Master Cháng Bǎi: the obstructions include timidity, covering, discursive thought, and self-conceit — removing them with antidotes naturally brings gladness.

quiz.q: Marks, thoughts, and secondary afflictions "are suffering, not noble, leading to no benefit." What chain of dangers does Master Cháng Bǎi trace?
options: no absorption, no wisdom, no cutting affliction — more karma, more suffering
quiz.why: "Therefore, these marks, discursive thoughts, and secondary afflictions are suffering, not the state of the noble ones, and lead to what is without benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: without absorption, wisdom can't grow; without wisdom, affliction can't be cut; uncut affliction keeps making karma; karma brings the great suffering of birth and death.

quiz.q: The first of the six, "perception of marklessness" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say it counters?
options: the ten marks — no mark appearing in the mind
quiz.why: "First, the perception of marklessness. Second, within marklessness, the perception of no function." Master Cháng Bǎi: there were ten marks; now no mark appears in the mind — that is the perception of marklessness, exactly countering the ten marks.

quiz.q: The sixth, "the bliss of cessation free of affliction" — is it the noble state, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: no affliction disturbing — but not yet the noble state
quiz.why: "Fifth, the perception of tranquility. Sixth, within tranquility, the perception of the bliss of cessation, free of every affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: when affliction doesn't disturb you, that is called the perception of the bliss of cessation — but it doesn't mean the noble state.

quiz.q: Grasping brightness — lamp, fire, sun, moon. What does Master Cháng Bǎi caution about the sun?
options: best at sunset — noon sun is too strong and hurts the eyes
quiz.why: "The brightness of a lamp, of a great fire, of the sun's disk, or of the moon's disk." Master Cháng Bǎi: if contemplating the sun, sunset is best; the noon sun is too strong and unsuitable — it can harm the eyes.

quiz.q: If unable to visit a charnel ground, "grasp marks rendered in painting, wood, or stone." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say of painting?
options: painters render discoloration, decay, up to the bone-chain in colours
quiz.why: "If you are unable to go to a charnel ground, you should instead grasp such marks as rendered in painting, wood, or stone." Venerable Miào Jìng: a painter uses all kinds of colours and brushes to paint discoloration, decay, up through the bone-chain.
